Who these notes are for

This handout introduces the electricity foundations needed for Edexcel GCSE Physics: charge, current, potential difference, resistance and measurements in circuits.

Twelve teaching sections contain diagrams, core concepts, worked examples, exam tips and numbered exercise sets with subquestions. The final four pages give worked solutions and classroom marking points, including guidance for circuit drawings.

16 pages · 12 exercise sets · Worked solutions

Topics covered

  • Atomic structure, charge and standard circuit symbols
  • Sensors, diodes, switches and complete circuits
  • Potential difference as energy per coulomb and E = QV
  • Voltmeter connections and ideal meter resistance
  • Current, Q = It, electron drift and conventional current
  • Ammeters, series current and conservation of charge at junctions
  • Resistance, V = IR and mixed circuit calculations

A focused electricity handout, not a complete GCSE Physics course. This is an independent Study with Dr resource, not an official Pearson Edexcel publication or examination mark scheme. Existing source and diagram credits are retained.

Key ideas at a glance

Distinguish current and potential difference

Current is charge passing per second: I = Q/t. Potential difference is energy transferred per coulomb: V = E/Q. Charge is conserved; a component transfers energy rather than using up current.

Connect meters correctly

An ammeter goes in series and ideally has zero resistance. A voltmeter goes in parallel across the selected component and ideally has infinite resistance, so it draws no current.

Convert units before calculating

Use amperes rather than milliamperes and seconds rather than minutes in Q = It. For a 20 Ω resistor across 4.0 V for five minutes, I = 0.20 A, Q = 60 C and E = 240 J.
